question: Why must an experience be accepted as established by self-awareness even if not known that way at determination?
premises: At the time of later determination, the experience is not known in the same immediate way.
The experience is nevertheless established by self-awareness.
What is established by self-awareness must be accepted even when later conceptualized differently.
inference: Therefore self-awareness is the foundational proof of experience, prior to later determination.
plain_english: For at the time of later determination it is not known in that same way by self-awareness; even so, it must necessarily be accepted as established by self-awareness.
